reason: The bone framework has spaces awaiting mineral, so this directly addresses the strengthening goal.
expectation: The mineral will strengthen the bone framework.

alternatives.reason: Building a muscle is another visible goal, but strengthening the bones is equally direct.

effect: The mineral strengthened the bone while the elbow stayed movable; the muscles still need to be built and attached.
reaction: The contrast between hard bone and a movable joint makes sense.
reason: The goal calls for muscles made from cells and supporting tissue, so I’ll start with the front group.
expectation: The cells and supporting tissue will form the front muscle.

alternatives.reason: The back muscle also needs to be built.

effect: The front cells and supporting tissue formed the biceps, with tendon ends that can connect it to the skeleton.
reaction: The picture helps explain how separate cells become a whole muscle.
reason: The back muscle also needs to be built from its cells and supporting tissue.
expectation: The cells and supporting tissue will form the back muscle.

alternatives.reason: The biceps also needs to be attached, but I can build the other muscle first.

effect: Both muscles are built; their tendon ends show where they can attach to the skeleton.
reaction: Seeing the matching front and back structures makes their pairing clearer.
reason: The biceps needs to attach across the front of the elbow, as shown in its picture.
expectation: The biceps will attach to the arm skeleton.

alternatives.reason: The triceps also needs to attach on the other side.

effect: The biceps is attached across the front of the elbow; the triceps still needs to go on the back.
reaction: The arrows make the biceps' pull and the resulting bend clear.
reason: The triceps needs to attach to the opposite side of the same arm.
expectation: The triceps will attach behind the elbow, completing the opposing muscle pair.

effect: The triceps completed the arm assembly. The two views show how muscles pulling on opposite sides bend and straighten the elbow.
reaction: Seeing both movements side by side made the muscle pair’s purpose clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Attaching the triceps was most worthwhile because the two views connected the muscles’ positions to bending and straightening.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the back muscle repeated much of the front muscle’s construction, although both were needed.

surprise.text: The bone became hard while the existing elbow tissues stayed unmineralized and movable.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary; the pictures and goals made the pairings understandable.

continue.text: I would choose to continue to see how other body parts work together; the final arm assembly made the connections easy to follow.
